answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a slowly maturing reputation bond: like a glacier, it forms gradually through verified work and cannot be rushed. Each epoch, the network takes a pulse of on-chain activity, and accounts whose behavior is sudden, identical, or unlinked to prior work are throttled. New identities start in a nebula of low trust, earning full access only after sustained, costly participation, so spawning a thousand fake agents costs a thousand glaciers' worth of time.
